knowledgeAnswers.rationale: The lesson defines an incident to include a near miss, and says to record facts promptly and follow the reporting process.

When a required control or instruction is unavailable, the response order is to stop the affected task and protect yourself and others, then contact the right person. Work continues only after the instruction is given, so asking the client what to do is not the response.
The recognise an incident section says an incident can include injury, near miss, spill, property damage or an unsafe condition.

practicalCriteria: Identifies relevant hazards, scope and site conditions
Selects and explains suitable controls and methods
Performs the sequence without unsafe contamination transfer
Verifies the outcome and documents exceptions
Escalates situations outside training or authority
passRule: Assessor must observe every safety-critical criterion; any failure requires remediation and reassessment.
evidenceRequired: Record of procedure step 2: Distinguish immediate danger from a problem that can be safely isolated and reported.
Record of procedure step 6: Record what happened, where and when, who was notified and any immediate controls, without speculation or blame.
stopWorkCriteria: Stop work if procedure step 1 is not done: Recognise the event as an incident, which can include an injury, near miss, spill, property damage or unsafe condition.
Stop work if procedure step 2 is not done: Distinguish immediate danger from a problem that can be safely isolated and reported.
Stop work if procedure step 3 is not done: Stop the affected task and make the area safe before anything else.
